author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
review: The Great Gatsby by F. Scott Fitzgerald is a timeless masterpiece that explores the decadence and disillusionment of the Jazz Age. Set in the Roaring Twenties, the novel follows the mysterious Jay Gatsby and his obsession with a lost love. Narrated by Nick Carraway, the story explores wealth, love, ambition, and the American Dream. Fitzgerald's beautiful prose and unforgettable characters make this novel a powerful exploration of society and human desire.

author: Harper Lee
review: To Kill a Mockingbird is a powerful story about childhood, justice, prejudice, and morality. Through the eyes of Scout Finch, readers experience the social tensions of a small Southern town and witness her father Atticus Finch defend an innocent man. Harper Lee creates memorable characters while exploring important themes of racial injustice, compassion, and courage.

author: George Orwell
review: George Orwell's 1984 presents a frightening vision of a future controlled by an authoritarian government. Winston Smith lives under constant surveillance and struggles against a system that controls information, language, and even thought. The novel explores freedom, propaganda, political power, and individual identity, making it one of the most influential dystopian novels ever written.

author: J.D. Salinger
review: The Catcher in the Rye follows Holden Caulfield, a teenager struggling with loneliness, identity, and the confusing transition into adulthood. His journey through New York reveals his frustration with what he sees as the hypocrisy of the adult world. Salinger's distinctive voice and emotional storytelling make the novel a memorable exploration of adolescence and identity.

author: Jane Austen
review: Pride and Prejudice is a classic romantic novel centered around Elizabeth Bennet and the proud but fascinating Mr. Darcy. Jane Austen explores love, marriage, class, reputation, and social expectations with sharp humor and memorable characters. Elizabeth's journey toward understanding herself and Darcy makes the novel both entertaining and deeply insightful.

author: J.R.R. Tolkien
review: The Hobbit follows Bilbo Baggins, a peaceful hobbit whose ordinary life changes when he joins a group of dwarves on an exciting quest. Along the journey, Bilbo encounters trolls, elves, giant spiders, and the mysterious dragon Smaug. Tolkien combines adventure, friendship, courage, and fantasy to create a timeless story enjoyed by readers of all ages.

bookName: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone
author: J.K. Rowling
review: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone introduces readers to Harry Potter, an ordinary boy who discovers that he is actually a young wizard. At Hogwarts, Harry makes lifelong friends, learns about magic, and discovers secrets about his past. The combination of friendship, adventure, mystery, and magic makes this book an unforgettable fantasy classic.

author: Paulo Coelho
review: The Alchemist follows Santiago, a young shepherd who travels across the desert in search of a treasure he has dreamed about. Along the way, he meets people who teach him valuable lessons about courage, dreams, love, and discovering one's purpose. Paulo Coelho's simple yet philosophical storytelling encourages readers to follow their dreams and listen to their hearts.

author: Paula Hawkins
review: The Girl on the Train is a psychological thriller centered around Rachel, a woman who observes a seemingly perfect couple during her daily train journey. When something unexpected happens, Rachel becomes involved in a mystery filled with secrets, unreliable memories, and hidden relationships. Paula Hawkins creates a tense and suspenseful story that keeps readers questioning what is real.

author: Mary Shelley
review: Frankenstein is a fascinating Gothic novel about Victor Frankenstein, a young scientist who creates a living creature through a mysterious scientific experiment. Horrified by his creation, Victor abandons it, leading to tragic consequences. Mary Shelley explores ambition, responsibility, loneliness, scientific curiosity, and the consequences of trying to control nature.

author: Charlotte Brontë
review: Jane Eyre follows a strong and independent young woman who faces hardship, loneliness, and social limitations while searching for love and personal freedom. Charlotte Brontë creates a deeply emotional story filled with mystery, romance, and moral conflict. Jane's determination to remain true to herself makes the novel especially memorable.

author: Louisa May Alcott
review: Little Women tells the heartwarming story of the four March sisters as they grow up, discover their ambitions, and face the challenges of family and adulthood. Each sister has a unique personality and dream. The novel beautifully explores family, friendship, love, sacrifice, ambition, and personal growth.

author: Bram Stoker
review: Bram Stoker's Dracula is a landmark Gothic horror novel introducing readers to the mysterious Count Dracula. Told through journals, letters, and other documents, the story follows a group of characters as they attempt to confront an ancient supernatural evil. The novel combines horror, mystery, adventure, and suspense to create an unforgettable story.

author: Charles Dickens
review: A Tale of Two Cities is set during the turbulent period of the French Revolution and follows characters whose lives become connected through love, sacrifice, and political conflict. Charles Dickens presents a powerful story about injustice, social inequality, courage, and redemption. The dramatic historical setting gives the novel tremendous emotional impact.

author: Lewis Carroll
review: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland takes readers into a strange and imaginative world where ordinary rules no longer apply. Alice encounters unusual characters, impossible situations, and endless wordplay as she travels through Wonderland. Lewis Carroll's imaginative storytelling creates a playful adventure about curiosity, identity, logic, and growing up.

author: Oscar Wilde
review: The Picture of Dorian Gray explores beauty, morality, temptation, and the consequences of living without responsibility. Dorian Gray wishes to remain young while his portrait ages in his place, allowing him to pursue a life of pleasure without immediately seeing the effects of his actions. Oscar Wilde combines elegant writing with philosophical ideas to create a dark and thought-provoking story.

author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
review: Crime and Punishment follows Raskolnikov, a troubled young man who commits a serious crime and then struggles with guilt, fear, and the consequences of his actions. Dostoevsky explores morality, justice, poverty, guilt, and redemption through an intense psychological narrative. The novel offers a deep examination of the human mind and personal transformation.

author: Arthur Conan Doyle
review: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes introduces readers to the brilliant detective Sherlock Holmes and his loyal companion Dr. Watson. Through a collection of intriguing cases, Holmes uses observation, logic, and deduction to solve mysteries that initially seem impossible. The clever investigations and memorable characters make this collection an entertaining mystery classic.

author: J.R.R. Tolkien
review: The Lord of the Rings follows Frodo Baggins on a perilous journey to destroy a powerful ring before it can return to the hands of the Dark Lord Sauron. Joined by a fellowship of companions, Frodo travels across Middle-earth through danger, friendship, and sacrifice. Tolkien's richly imagined world and timeless themes of courage and hope have made this fantasy epic beloved by readers around the world.

author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
review: The Little Prince tells the story of a young traveler who visits different planets and learns about love, loneliness, friendship, and the way people see the world. Through his conversations with a pilot stranded in the desert, Saint-Exupéry offers a gentle, imaginative reflection on what truly matters in life. Its simple storytelling and thoughtful ideas resonate with readers of all ages.
